payload.text: Replace the smoothed maximum with an epigraph variable t and constraints (f*f)[k] <= t, fixing sum(f)=1. Optimize log(Q)-log(t), where Q=(2 sum(c²)+sum(c[k]c[k+1]))/3. Use sequential linearized subproblems with nonnegativity bounds and a trust region; accept steps only after exact rescoring.

Use constraint generation for the epigraph formulation. Start with representative near-maximal convolution lags, solve the restricted step, then compute the full convolution and add violated or newly near-active lags. Retain previously binding constraints until several accepted iterations show substantial slack.

Parameterize the incumbent by multiplicative weights on contiguous nonzero runs, preserving each run's internal profile. Split long runs into segments of at most 256 cells. Optimize these weights under fixed total mass before attempting cellwise polishing, retaining the original candidate as a fallback.

Estimate nonnegative multipliers on near-maximal convolution lags by minimizing the stationarity residual of the exact log-score, with multipliers summing to one. Use the resulting reduced gradient to rank support births and weight transfers, rather than selecting moves from a single maximizing lag.

Optimize proposed support births directly in nonnegative amplitudes rather than squared coordinates, whose derivatives vanish at zero. Add batches of zero cells ranked by reduced gradient, fund their mass from existing support, and jointly optimize birth amplitudes and donor weights inside a small trust region.

Test coordinated topology changes involving 4–32 nonzero runs simultaneously. Translate selected runs by small integer offsets while preserving their values and resolving collisions by addition. Bias selections toward weakly constrained runs, then jointly refit affected run weights and accept only exact-score improvements.

Evaluate every proposed search direction using a geometric grid of step sizes and the exact nonsmoothed score. Include steps much smaller than the optimizer's proposed step, and refine around the best bracket. This lets useful directions survive when a flat convolution plateau makes conventional smooth line searches unreliable.

Choose LogSumExp sharpness adaptively rather than by a fixed schedule. Normalize the convolution maximum to one, measure log(sum(exp(beta*(c-max(c)))))/beta, and increase beta until this excess is below a specified tolerance between 1e-8 and 1e-6. Reassess sharpness after substantial accepted moves.

Checkpoint exact scores throughout optimization, not only at stage boundaries. Rescore accepted iterates at least every five iterations, preserve the best exact candidate independently of optimizer state, and restart from that checkpoint after sustained deterioration. Allow continuation trajectories to deteriorate temporarily without losing intermediate improvements.

Explore mass redistribution between large spatial regions while preserving microscopic support. Partition the grid into 16–128 contiguous regions, multiply each region's existing values by an independent positive weight, and optimize the weights jointly. Repeat with shifted partition boundaries before returning to run-level refinement.

payload.formulation: Represent a candidate by its nonnegative amplitude vector. Optimize local amplitude perturbations through a linear-program epigraph for the convolution peak, adding violated lag constraints adaptively. The adapter exposes the amplitudes as the verifier's values; canonical warm starts remain accepted unchanged.

payload.text: Test mass-preserving resolution transfers of the incumbent up to the two-million-cell limit. Integrate its piecewise-constant density over new cells, then optimize newly available amplitudes, including initially zero cells. Compare several noninteger resolution ratios using exact verifier scores; retain the original unchanged and do not assume resampling preserves score.

Explore nonuniform spatial warps of the incumbent using 8–32 monotone movable breakpoints. Redistribute mass by interval overlap, allowing occupied blocks and empty bands to change widths independently. Search both small and substantial warp proposals, refit nonnegative amplitudes afterward, and retain candidates only by exact nonsmoothed score.

payload.rationale: Recent gains are far below the record threshold, so further polishing alone is unlikely to suffice. Restructuring has the strongest observed operator results, while the validated amplitude/epigraph island remains untested. Shift budget toward that island and structural exploration while retaining the incumbent island. Test resolution and geometry changes as new directions; do not assume the claimed upsampling invariance or revive the refuted constraint-generation approach.

payload.hypothesis: Adding a mass-orthogonal quadratic shape mode to each packet will improve the verified score more than amplitude-and-tilt polishing alone within the same time budget.

Adding a mass-orthogonal quadratic mode to each packet's amplitude-and-tilt basis will expose coherent within-packet curvature adjustments and improve the exact verified score beyond the parent's approximately 1e-9 gains.
Shifting packet boundaries between continuation stages will remove fixed-partition restrictions and produce an additional verified gain of roughly 1e-9 to 1e-8.

payload.formulation: Represent candidates as nonnegative cell masses. Search conservative nearest-neighbor transport fields coherent within occupied packets, including packet dilation, contraction, and spatially varying translation. Optimize transport strength using the exact quadratic convolution along each ray. The adapter exposes the resulting cell masses to the unchanged verifier.

Represent a candidate as a nonnegative sample ring, a cut index, and a reflection mode. The adapter either rotates the ring at the cut or reflects its prefix or suffix. This makes large packet-order changes explicit while preserving the original grid and avoiding interpolation. Canonical warm starts remain accepted.

Represent the function as nonoverlapping occupied packets on an integer grid. Each packet stores its starting index and its sample values; omitted cells are zero. Search conservative packet remeshings that vary widths and anchoring while preserving each packet's mass, and compare finite convex mixtures using their exact quadratic convolutions.

payload.text: For a feasible mass-preserving direction h, precompute f*f, f*h, and h*h. Evaluate convolution along the ray as f*f + 2t(f*h) + t²(h*h), avoiding repeated FFTs. Search the full feasible interval with a geometric grid and refine several promising brackets using the exact nonsmoothed score; retain the original as fallback.

Test finite support changes rather than only infinitesimal polishing. Move 0.1%, 0.3%, 1%, and 3% of total mass from occupied packets into narrow nonnegative packets at empty-band locations. Jointly refit donor and recipient amplitudes, preserve the unmodified incumbent, and rank completed trials by exact verifier score.

payload.rationale: Recent gains are orders of magnitude below the required 1e-5, while all 125 evaluations went to I1 and four validated alternative representations remain untested. Redirect most evaluations toward those islands, preserve a smaller incumbent-polishing budget, and modestly favor reformulation over exhausted local operators. Flatten parent selection to reduce repeated exploitation of nearly identical incumbents. Use exact ray searches and finite support changes to test escapes without relying on a smoothed peak or infinitesimal improvements.

payload.hypothesis: A cutting-plane minimax search over coordinated packet transport will escape the fixed-support plateau and gain at least 1e-5 while preserving the incumbent if unsuccessful.

payload.text: For epigraph amplitude steps, enforce the linearized peak bound over every convolution lag using matrix-free products or streamed constraint blocks. Do not retain only currently near-active lags. Rescore the full nonlinear convolution after each proposed step, and shrink the trust region when predicted improvement fails.

Run checkpointed basin-hopping trajectories using packet-order changes, reflections, and substantial support moves. Allow temporary exact-score deterioration within each trajectory, then refit amplitudes before comparing endpoints. Preserve the global incumbent separately and restart from structurally distinct endpoints rather than repeatedly polishing the same support.

payload.rationale: Recent gains are several orders of magnitude below the required 1e-5, and three evaluated islands have converged to essentially the same score. Further local polishing has little demonstrated value. Redirect most effort toward the untested epigraph and packet-order formulations, while retaining incumbent-based searches as controls. Favor restructuring and reformulation over fresh starts and refinement. Do not revive the refuted constraint-generation approach; require full-lag checks.

payload.text: Separate block masses from within-block mass fractions at block sizes 2, 4, 8, and 16. Hold block masses fixed initially and optimize nonnegative fractions from randomized asymmetric starts, then release both scales jointly. Test finite departures from uniform fractions, not only infinitesimal steps. Preserve the incumbent and compare endpoints using the exact verifier.

Choose hybridization parents by structural distance as well as score. Normalize mass, account for translation and reflection equivalences, and compare coarse mass profiles and support masks. Reject numerically identical parent pairs. Recombine complementary spatial regions with several boundary choices, then jointly refit regional weights and amplitudes before exact endpoint comparison.

Launch independent coarse-grid searches without inheriting the incumbent support. Retain structurally distinct solutions even when their coarse scores are lower. Lift several finalists through increasing resolutions using mass-preserving resampling and amplitude optimization, never exceeding two million cells. Judge success only after full-resolution exact rescoring, keeping the original incumbent separately.
